title: ActionCodec: What Makes for Good Action Tokenizers
abstract: arXiv:2602.15397v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models leveraging the native autoregressive paradigm of Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have demonstrated superior instruction-following and training efficiency. Central to this paradigm is action tokenization, yet its design has primarily focused on reconstruction fidelity, failing to address its direct impact on VLA optimization. Consequently, the fundamental question of \textit{what makes for good action tokenizers} remains unanswered. In this paper, we bridge this gap by establishing design principles specifically from the perspective of VLA optimization. We identify a set of best practices based on information-theoretic insights, including maximized temporal token overlap, minimized vocabulary redundancy, enhanced multimodal mutual information, and token independence. translated_title: ActionCodec：什么造就了好的动作分词器
translated_abstract: 利用视觉-语言模型（VLM）原生自回归范式的视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型已展现出卓越的指令遵循能力和训练效率。该范式的核心在于动作分词，然而其设计主要聚焦于重构保真度，未能解决其对VLA优化的直接影响。因此，“什么造就了好的动作分词器”这一根本问题至今仍未得到解答。在本文中，我们通过专门从VLA优化的角度建立设计原则来弥合这一差距。我们基于信息论洞察确定了一组最佳实践，包括最大化的时序token重叠、最小化的词表冗余、增强的多模态互信息以及token独立性。在这些原则的指导下，我们提出了ActionCodec——一个高性能的动作分词器，能够显著提升机器人（学习性能）。
tldr: 本文从VLA优化的角度出发，基于信息论洞察建立了动作分词器的最佳设计原则（时序token重叠最大化、词表冗余最小化、多模态互信息增强、token独立性），并据此提出了高性能动作分词器ActionCodec。
en_tdlr: This paper establishes design principles for action tokenizers from the perspective of VLA optimization based on information-theoretic insights, and introduces ActionCodec, a high-performance action tokenizer guided by these principles.
